open_hypotheses.claim: Provider substitution is an architectural equivalence, not a behavioral identity. The Claude runtime preserves its existing behavior (reference); alternative providers (Ollama with deepseek-v4-flash:cloud, qwen2.5:3b, ...) are *characterized* against Claude on benchmark-001, not required to imitate Claude output. A lower-cost / lower-latency / slightly-different-dialogue is an engineering tradeoff, not a regression.
open_hypotheses.measured_from: benchmark-001-grounding run output across (runtime, model, profile) combinations; compared via outcome distribution, mean tension, latency, cost, mean_self_similarity, witness_attempts/witness_turns (for Reflective).

accepted_decisions: GenerationRuntime is the provider-neutral runtime protocol. The dialectical engine depends on GenerationRuntime, not on TextGenerating/ClaudeCLIGenerator. (ADR-009.)

GenerationRuntime is composed over a GenerationTransport (HTTP / subprocess / local-process). Adding a model behind an existing transport is a configuration change, not a Swift type. (ADR-009 invariant #3.)

TextGenerating is preserved as a legacy compatibility shim during the transition. The harness, app, and tests migrate incrementally; TextGenerating is deprecated once nothing depends on it. (ADR-009.)
Prompt profiles are repository resources (Markdown files under Sources/BCICloudBridge/Prompts/), not code on the runtime. Ownership belongs to the dialectical engine. (ADR-009 invariant #1.)
The runtime SHALL NOT modify semantic intent: no prompt rewriting, no temperature adjustment, no hidden system prompts, no response interpretation. (ADR-009 invariant #2.)

The runtime is capability-advertised. RuntimeCapabilities { tokenCounting: Bool, streaming: Bool, logProbs: Bool, ... } is published by each conformer. Optional methods (estimateTokens, etc.) are best-effort. (ADR-009 invariant #4.)

Benchmark governance is a separate document (docs/architecture/benchmark-governance.md), referenced not defined in ADR-009. Canonical benchmarks are immutable. Provider comparisons MUST use canonical benchmark artifacts. (ADR-009 invariant #5; benchmark-governance.md.)

ClaudeCLIGenerator remains the reference implementation for the dialectical engine. Provider substitution does not relax the no-network-at-runtime principle; each non-local transport is its own opt-in surface and its own banner disclosure.
Provider-substitution equivalence is architectural, not behavioral. Characterize tradeoffs; do not require model output equality. (Keep-bar.)

Benchmark-001-grounding (docs/seeds/benchmarks/benchmark-001-grounding.txt) is the canonical cross-provider evaluation input. Committed on seed-003 / e1eb7f4; first-drafted on worldmodel/overnight-transform-ab. Cross-provider runs use identical input, identical prompt profile, identical interaction style; only runtime, model, and generation parameters may differ.

Runtime selection precedence: CLI flag (`--runtime <name>`) > environment variable (`NEURALCOMPOSE_RUNTIME=<name>`) > Claude (default). UI selection (e.g. an in-app picker) is a separate Sources/NeuralComposeApp/ change, out of scope for this branch.
rejected_decisions: Per-provider Swift conformers (one DeepSeekGenerator, one MinimaxGenerator, ...). Rejected in favor of transport-level conformers with model-as-configuration; per-provider conformers duplicate the transport code for no benefit.

Mandatory tokenize() on the protocol. Rejected in favor of capability-advertised token counting (RuntimeCapabilities.tokenCounting) and best-effort estimateTokens() that returns nil when unsupported. The Claude CLI does not expose token counts; requiring it would force every Claude conformer to synthesize them.

PromptProfile as Swift structs in code. Rejected in favor of Markdown files under Sources/BCICloudBridge/Prompts/. The dialectical engine loads them at startup; a Swift struct could be regenerated from the Markdown if needed. (This decision is preliminary; if a future branch finds the loader cost prohibitive, a Swift-struct variant is a small reversible change.)
Burning an ADR number for benchmark governance. Rejected in favor of docs/architecture/benchmark-governance.md. ADR-009 references it; the policy lives there, decoupled from runtime architecture.
pending_questions: What is the correct ergonomic for prompt loading at startup? (Once-per-process load, per-turn load, hot-reload in dev? — Implementation detail; default = once-per-process; revisit if observed cost is wrong.)
Does the generator fingerprint need to be signed for tamper-resistance in adversarial settings? (Out of scope for this branch; current shape is informational, not cryptographic.)

How are the multi-modal future runtimes (text-to-image, etc.) shaped? (Deferred; GenerationRuntime is a generation contract, not a language contract, so a future multimodal conformer is a runtime-not-protocol concern.)

experiments.runs: profile in {focused, reflective, contemplative} x runtime in {claude-cli, ollama:deepseek-v4-flash:cloud, ollama:qwen2.5:3b} x seeds {0, 1, 2}
experiments.keep_bar: Claude reference behavior preserved; alternative providers characterized, not required to imitate. A null result (alternative provider regresses seed-002 numbers) is a valid, recorded outcome — not a failure.
